title: ¿Verdad o Mentira?
sub: Truth or Lie? · Grades 5–8 · Spanish · 30 minutes
objective: Students will acquire vocabulary related to truth/deception (*verdad, mentira, real, falso, creer, ver*), practice expressing opinions using “Creo que…” and “Pienso que…”, and connect language learning to critical thinking about visual media.
materials: Spirit photography example from Mini Museum
Vocabulary cards or projected word list
connection: **Option 1 — Visit:** Students describe artifacts using Spanish: “Veo una foto. Creo que es falsa.”

steps.title: ¿Qué ven tus ojos?
script: Display an optical illusion. Point to your eyes.
“¿Qué ven tus ojos?” (What do your eyes see?) — Have students call out what they see. Then reveal the illusion. “¡Tus ojos te engañan!” (Your eyes trick you!)

screen.caption: ¿Qué ven tus ojos?
screen.alt: A checkerboard with a brown cylinder casting a shadow across it; square A sits outside the shadow, square B inside it

steps.purpose: Students call out what they see before the reveal.

steps.title: ¡Tus ojos te engañan!
script: “¿Qué ven tus ojos?” (What do your eyes see?) — Have students call out what they see. Then reveal the illusion. “¡Tus ojos te engañan!” (Your eyes trick you!)

screen.caption: ¡Tus ojos te engañan!
screen.alt: The checkerboard taken away: squares A and B alone on black, the same gray

steps.title: Key vocabulary
script: Introduce key vocabulary: *ver, los ojos, engañar, la verdad, la mentira.* Use gestures and visuals.
steps.purpose: The first five words, with gestures and visuals.
students: Say each word with its gesture.

steps.title: La verdad y la mentira
script: Present vocabulary with Total Physical Response (TPR) and comprehensible input:
steps.purpose: All ten words, heard and seen.

steps.title: Total Physical Response
steps.purpose: A gesture for each word, so the whole class answers at once.
students: Do the gesture as you say the word.

steps.title: Quick practice
script: **Quick practice:** Show images, students respond “¡Verdad!” or “¡Mentira!”
steps.purpose: A quick check before the Mini Museum connection.

steps.title: La Fotografía de Espíritus
script: “En 1862, un fotógrafo dijo: ‘Puedo fotografiar fantasmas.’ Muchas personas creyeron. ¿Es verdad o mentira?” (In 1862, a photographer said: ‘I can photograph ghosts.’ Many people believed. Is it truth or lie?)

screen.question: En 1862, un fotógrafo dijo: ‘Puedo fotografiar fantasmas.’ Muchas personas creyeron. ¿Es verdad o mentira?

steps.purpose: A real fake from history, in simple Spanish.

steps.title: Partner practice
script: **Partner practice:** Students discuss using sentence frames: “Creo que es mentira porque…” (I believe it’s a lie because…). Heritage speakers can help partners with vocabulary.
steps.purpose: Partners give their opinion with a sentence frame; heritage speakers help with vocabulary.

steps.title: ¿Verdad o Mentira? Game
script: Show 4–5 images (mix of real and manipulated). Students hold up VERDAD or MENTIRA cards. After each: “¿Por qué crees eso?” (Why do you believe that?) — Students respond using sentence frames.
steps.purpose: Students judge real and manipulated images, and say why.
students: Creo que es… / Pienso que es…

steps.title: Reflection
script: “No todo lo que vemos es verdad. Debemos pensar antes de creer.” (Not everything we see is truth. We should think before believing.)
**Exit ticket:** Students write one sentence using new vocabulary.

screen.question: No todo lo que vemos es verdad. Debemos pensar antes de creer.

steps.purpose: One sentence to remember, then the exit ticket.
students: Write one sentence using new vocabulary.
